subject: Meteorology
title: Lapse Rates
description: A quick win: understand Lapse Rates.

hook.text: Temperature usually drops as you go higher—but the rate of that drop tells us a lot about the atmosphere.

buildup.text: The environmental lapse rate is the actual temperature change with altitude—it varies from place to place.

discovery.text: On average, the troposphere cools about 6.5°C per km—but this can change dramatically with weather conditions.

twist.text: Sometimes temperature increases with height instead—this reversal is called a temperature inversion.

climax.text: Inversions trap pollution, fog, and smog near the surface—they act like a lid on the lower atmosphere.

punchline.text: When temperatures flip, so does air quality.

quiz.question: What is the average environmental lapse rate in the troposphere?
